title: POC hosting decision kickoff - Neptune Logistics
summary: Kickoff to scope a 6-week POC to evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment. Next steps agreed: send benchmark template, share security pack, schedule benchmark run and internal procurement sync.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Aaron Blake (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Neptune CTO), Lena Ortiz (Head of ML), Tom Hayes (Infra Lead), Sofia Kim (Product)

Auto-generated sections (may be imperfect):
Summary: Kickoff POC to evaluate hosting modes and success criteria.
Topics: success metric definitions, expected qps, bench plan, timelines, compliance constraints.

Transcript: 
[00:00:05] Aaron: hey everyone, thanks for carving time. this is Aaron from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, joining with Maya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:00:12] Raj: doing well, thanks. goal for us is pretty simple, we need to pick a hosting approach for inference for our route-optimization assistant, and we'd like a POC to validate latency and cost tradeoffs.
[00:00:22] Maya: great, thanks Raj. quick agenda: align on success criteria, collect workload numbers (qps, payload sizes), plan a baseline benchmark, and flag any security must-haves that would rule out hosted. sound ok?
[00:00:30] Lena: yes that works. i'll kick off with the model side — our assistant does short prompts, average token length ~120 tokens, about 60% of calls are synchronous request-response for route calc, the rest are async batched jobs. peak qps is around 120 at rush, steady is closer to 18 to 25.
[00:00:48] Tom: infra side, we are pretty strict on data controls. we have customers in EU and APAC that require data residency; we also need KMS integration and audit logs to meet our internal compliance.
[00:00:57] Aaron: quick clarifying question — when you say data residency, is it payload-level or metadata-level? like can we redact or is full custody required?
[00:01:05] Raj: primarily payload. some customers contractually require that PII never leaves an EU data-center — so that would push us to either Dedicated in region or fully private deployment.
[00:01:15] Maya: understood. two quick framing points: Hosted is fastest to spin up and best for iteration, Dedicated gives you reserved capacity in a region with stronger isolation and predictable throughput, and Private is customer-managed — best for strict residency and on-prem constraints but longer lead time to provision.
[00:01:31] Sofia: cost wise, we've been running internal cost models that show hosted is cheaper early but at scale dedicated or private might be more predictable. we need a cost-per-100k-requests metric.
[00:01:40] Aaron: noted. for the POC success criteria, customers typically use a combination: 95th percentile latency target, accuracy/regression tolerance vs baseline model, cost per 100k requests, and operability e.g., rollout time and autoscaling behavior. what's a reasonable 95th pct target for you?
[00:01:55] Lena: for interactive flows, 95th pct < 400ms ideally. for async batched jobs we can tolerate higher.
[00:02:03] Maya: ok 400ms 95th, thats helpful. two nuances — model size and KV cache can influence tail latency a lot. do you have a pinned model family or are you open to trimmed/quantized variants?
[00:02:14] Raj: currently experimenting with an open LLM tuned in-house, approx 13B weights; quantized variants are an option if quality hold.
[00:02:22] Aaron: good. for the benchmark plan i propose: week 1 we run synthetic workload that mirrors your qps profile (burst and steady), measure token throughput, 95p latency, and cost using Redwood hosted runtime. week 2 we run on Dedicated in eu-west region with same workload. if data residency blocks hosted for eu traffic, we can route synthetic to dedicated for eu flows. if you want private, we estimate an extra 6-10 weeks to provision depending on on-prem readiness.
[00:02:46] Tom: that provisioning estimate aligns with us — private will hit procurement and network config takes time. can Dedicated meet the KMS requirement?
[00:02:54] Maya: yes Dedicated can integrate with customer-managed keys (KMS) and we provide audit logs. Private gives you full control. Hosted also supports BYOK in some regions but that depends on legal and DPA terms.
[00:03:07] Raj: what's the sizing exercise look like? we have peak 120 qps with 120 token average.
[00:03:12] Maya: we'll need representative payloads and some telemetry — lumbering request distributions, percent of calls with long context, and concurrency patterns. with that we produce a recommended instance mix, expected throughput per GPU, and cost projection compared across hosted/dedicated/private.
[00:03:27] Sofia: what's our expected burn during the POC? we have limited credits for infra.
[00:03:31] Aaron: we typically size bench runs to be efficient — synthetic burst tests and steady-state runs, we can constrain token budget. the benchmark template we'll share includes a cost estimator so you can see projected bill for the planned runs.
[00:03:43] Raj: another gating item is SLA. enterprise flows need 99.9% availability for critical endpoints. does Dedicated include SLA?
[00:03:50] Maya: Dedicated packages come with SLA options, yes. Hosted has SLAs for paid tiers too; Private SLAs are part of the enterprise contract and depend on support level.
[00:03:59] [00:04:02] Aaron: i'd like to call out regression testing. if you plan to use quantized models or alternate kernels, we need to include quality checks comparing outputs to your golden set. Lena, can you provide ~200 golden prompts for that?
[00:04:12] Lena: yes we can — i'll export a golden set with scoring rubric. note some prompts are geo-specific so we'll mark that.
[00:04:20] Tom: network topology — would you require VPC peering to run Dedicated in our account?
[00:04:24] Maya: Dedicated can be provisioned either in Redwood-managed VPCs with dedicated capacity that peered to your network, or as private deployment into your VPC for fully customer-controlled networking. peering requirements and firewall rules will be in the runbook we share.
[00:04:37] Raj: any hidden performance caveats? like cold-starts or KV cache warm-up?
[00:04:41] Maya: yes cold starts can add tail latency — that's managed with warm pools and continuous batching. KV cache warm-up matters if you have long conversations; for route-optimization less so but we will measure it.
[00:04:53] Aaron: timeline proposal: 1) send benchmark template and runbook (Aaron/Maya) by 2027-04-14; 2) Neptune supplies telemetry and golden prompts by 2027-04-16; 3) baseline hosted or dedicated synthetic run week of 2027-04-19; 4) analyze results and then recommend final hosting mode by 2027-05-03. does that feel realistic?
[00:05:10] Raj: yes sounds good. procurement will need an estimate and contract terms; can you share ballpark pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[00:05:17] Aaron: we'll include ballpark committed capacity pricing in the doc — note that Dedicated has a monthly reserved component so we model both committed and burst scenarios.
[00:05:25] Sofia: any differences in observability and tracing we should know?
[00:05:28] Maya: all modes expose token-level latency and cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and traces. Private can stream logs to your splunk/elk if required.
[00:05:36] Raj: what about fallback behaviors — if Dedicated is saturated, can requests transparently go to Hosted?
[00:05:41] Maya: yes that's part of smart routing — you can configure policy-based fallback to a compatible model variant in another tier/region. that has implications for data controls and consent, so we'll highlight tradeoffs.
[00:05:53] Tom: last question — do you have customers doing hybrid routing by geography? topologies similar to what we need?
[00:05:58] Aaron: yes we've seen a few logistics and fintech customers route eu traffic to dedicated in eu-west and rest to hosted. we can share anonymized references.
[00:06:05] [longer section elided for brevity but reflects ~58m call]
[00:35:12] Raj: just to reiterate, our decision drivers are 1) data residency 2) latency 95p < 400ms 3) cost predictability 4) ops complexity. if Dedicated hits all but cost is marginally higher it's probably acceptable.
[00:35:25] Maya: agreed. we'll score each mode against these drivers in the deliverable.
[00:35:30] Aaron: ok quick recap of immediate actions then: we'll share the benchmark template and a runbook, Redwood will run an initial synthetic benchmark, Neptune will provide telemetry and golden prompts, and we'll regroup after the baseline results.
[00:35:44] Lena: can you also include a simple A/B quality test plan so we can evaluate quantization impact?
[00:35:49] Maya: yes we'll include that — we'll run baseline float weights vs a 4-bit quantized variant and report BLEU/ROUGE-style deltas and any semantic drift examples.
[00:35:59] Sofia: timeline for the security deep-dive? procurement will want to see SOC2 scope and DPA.
[00:36:04] Aaron: propose week of 2027-04-26 — we'll invite security and solutions engineering to that call.
[00:36:11] Raj: sounds good. anything else?
[00:36:14] Tom: just one more nit — logging retention. we'll need audit logs retained for 1 year.
[00:36:19] Maya: that's fine, retention is configurable in Dedicated and Private; Hosted has tiers for retention. we'll document specifics.
[00:36:26] Aaron: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll send the template and runbook today / tomorrow and set the benchmark slot.
[00:36:33] Raj: thanks all.

End of transcript.

Post-call notes: Redwood to produce a short decision rubric comparing Hosted/Dedicated/Private across latency, cost, compliance, and time-to-production. Customer requested benchmark template, golden prompts, and security pack.
